assessment: A strong episode for the format. The reveal runs 5:54 to 10:36 and Mike explains the reasoning behind almost every choice, which is what makes a good Short: a narrow island because a standard one would not fit, tape lighting instead of pucks, a shallow vented microwave so the cabinets above can be taller, and open shelving instead of a pantry with the depth argument spelled out. Eight distinct camera setups in the reveal, so there is no need to cut twice from any one of them. Cost slide at 11:10, fenced off.

the Project Statistics slide. Mike's spoken outro from 10:36 plays over clean kitchen footage and the location audio is muted, so the picture is usable

project_context.summary: Kitchen and family room remodel in a house with a small kitchen footprint. White oak cabinets with a grey stain, a narrower than standard island with the bins inside it, under cabinet tape lighting, a shallow vented microwave, full depth adjustable shelving where two closets used to be, drawers instead of doors, and the half wall replaced with a matching white oak railing.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut entirely from 5:54 to 10:44, the finished reveal. No before footage and no install footage.
notes: Every frame is the finished kitchen.
Seven camera setups used, none twice.

shorts.full_vo:
This kitchen in the Blue House is done, and it is a completely different room. The island is narrower than standard, because a normal one would not fit. No overhang, and the garbage cans live inside it.

Under the cabinets we switched to tape lighting. A narrow LED band, unobtrusive and very bright. The microwave is the shallow kind, and we vented it outside. Which leaves room for taller cabinets above it.

Where two closets used to be, there is full depth adjustable shelving. A pantry is two feet deep, but its shelves are only sixteen inches. And drawers instead of doors, so nothing hides at the back.

The half wall came out and became a white oak railing, stained to match. Which makes the whole room feel bigger. White oak cabinets, grey stain, and a floor that is fully waterproof.
